item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 081150
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Tue Sep 8 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Lowell, located just north-northwest of Lihue, Kauai, and on
Tropical Storm Marie, located several hundred miles west of Punta
Eugenia, Mexico.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a broad area of low
pressure located several hundred miles southwest of southwestern
Mexico are showing signs of organization. Gradual development of
this system is likely, and a tropical depression is expected to
form later this week while the system moves generally
west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Well South of the Southern Tip of Baja California:
An area of low pressure is forecast to develop several hundred miles
south of the southern tip of Baja California this weekend or early
next week. Some slow development is possible as this system moves
generally west-northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Kelly

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Marie Public Advisory Number 30
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Tue Sep 08 2026 
630 
WTPZ33 KNHC 081437
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Post-Tropical Cyclone Marie Advisory Number  30
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 AM PDT Tue Sep 08 2026
 
...MARIE BECOMES A POST TROPICAL CYCLONE...
...THIS IS THE LAST ADVISORY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...25.8N 127.4W
ABOUT 770 MI...1240 KM W OF PUNTA EUGENIA MEXICO
ABOUT 780 MI...1260 KM SW OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Post-Tropical Cyclone Marie
was located near latitude 25.8 North, longitude 127.4 West. The
post-tropical cyclone is moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph
(15 km/h) and is forecast to turn to the northwest over the next 
day or so. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts.
Steady weakening is expected to continue, and Marie is forecast to 
dissipate in a couple of days. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of
the coast of the Baja California Peninsula and southern California
for the next couple of days.  These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.  Please consult
products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip current
risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on this system. For additional information on the remnant low 
please see High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather 
Service, under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN01 KWBC, and 
on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Kelly

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Forecast Discussion Number 29
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Tue Sep 08 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 080849
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Marie Discussion Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM PDT Tue Sep 08 2026
 
The satellite presentation of Marie continues to degrade as the 
cyclone continues to weaken. What is the left of the deep convection 
is very minimal and limited to the southeastern quadrant of the 
storm. The latest TAFB Dvorak fix came in at T2.5/35 kt, and the 
objective satellite estimates from UW-CIMSS are in the range of 
30-44 kt. The most recent scatterometer pass showed that there are 
still some 35-kt winds and given that this pass only partially 
captured the storm, there could still be some stronger winds. 
Therefore, the initial intensity has been lowered to 40 kt for this 
advisory.
 
The storm continues its slow west-northwestward trek with an initial 
motion estimate of around 300/7 kt. Marie is expected to turn more 
northwestward and move within the flow between a ridge extending 
westward from the southwestern U.S. and a cutoff low to the west of 
the tropical cyclone. The current NHC track forecast is similar to 
the previous forecast track, and is close to the corrected model 
consensus.
 
Marie is expected to move over cooler waters for the next day or so, 
and based on the decreasing convection, it seems likely that the 
storm will become post-tropical within the next 24 h. Unless deep 
convection is able to return to the cyclone soon, Marie's 
post-tropical transition could occur even earlier than the official 
forecast. The current NHC intensity forecast is very similar to the 
previous intensity forecast.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  08/0900Z 25.5N 126.6W   40 KT  45 MPH
 12H  08/1800Z 26.3N 127.5W   35 KT  40 MPH
 24H  09/0600Z 27.9N 128.6W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 36H  09/1800Z 29.8N 129.9W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 48H  10/0600Z 32.1N 131.4W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW

$$
Forecaster Katz/Gibbs
